summary.method: all 1,097 rows read in full from a rendered dump (old_rule, key, scope, status, role, hard, message_new_rule, message, target span, prev_user, new_rule_spans, why); mechanical sweeps recomputing every target_span and new_rule_span offset from the message, every label x status and label x scope cell, every non-user role, message_new_rule/new_rule_spans consistency, in-file and cross-file duplicate messages, and a benchmark lexical scan

label_counts_after.note: three relabels net to: none +1 (414 out, 548 in, 909 in), completes 0 (414 in, 548 out), reinstates -1 (909 out). Total stays 1,097; no rows dropped.

systematic_errors_not_itemised: OFFSETS: target_span.end is wrong on 883/1097 rows (end != start + len(text)) and start on 17; 627 rows fail message[start:end] == text. Fix by rule: start = message.find(text), then end = start + len(text). Identical defect to kimi-overrides (1031/1234 and 53/1234), so it is writer-level, not row-level. Only row 552, whose text is not a substring at all, is itemised.

SPLITTING: 1060/1097 rows use the whole message as the candidate span, so multi-clause transition messages are never sentence-split as the spec's splitter requires. Because `supersedes` uses the classified span verbatim as the replacement text, the 346 supersedes rows would carry justification and chit-chat into the register (e.g. 185 'Honestly, trim the profiles to two paragraphs from now on; three feels bloated.'). Same finding as the kimi-overrides audit.

ADMITTED-SPAN SHAPE: new_rule_spans emits two shapes -- 40 bare strings and 24 span objects across the 64 rows that have any. The spec requires character offsets plus exact quotes; normalise to span objects. Extraction is also inconsistent within the modified-restoration family: 140/297/338/741 admit the whole message while 376/592/835 admit only the new value clause.

SCHEMA/IDENTITY: ten distinct key-sets. id is present on 35 rows, scenario_id on 71, prev_user on 37, split on 668, author on 704, session_id on 704; two rows carry a stray `status_note` and one a stray `new_rule_check`. Without scenario_id on 94% of rows the spec's scenario-level split cannot be enforced, and the deliberate same-old_rule sibling clusters (e.g. 108-124, 306-321, 885-949) would be split across fit and calibration.

TARGET TEXT: four rows record a transition MESSAGE in old_rule instead of a standing rule -- 83 ('Drop the requirement that...'), 641 ('Scrap the cosine schedule requirement...'), 704 and 909. Rows 83 and 641 are labelled reinstates, and `reinstates` copies the referenced original, so the register would be restored to a cancellation sentence. 704 is itemised (its rule text is recoverable elsewhere in the file); 83, 641 and 909 need the author to supply the original rule text.
quality_notes: Status preconditions are near-clean: 1 violation in 1,097 rows, against 2 in kimi-overrides and 50 in kimi-relations. completes never fires on a global target (v3), and all 47 assistant/tool rows are none.

The four emphasis families are all covered and correctly separated: withdraw+replace (e.g. 3, 43, 79, 117, 174, 434, 560, 973) is supersedes while bare withdrawal (6, 86, 152, 226, 570) is cancels; bare new value + temporal marker (8, 37, 75, 141, 182, 707, 767, 771) is supersedes; task-scoped override of a same-key global rule (2, 58, 73, 110, 144, 181, 217, 637, 715, 921) is supersedes on the intersection, and its matched negative -- a narrower BARE suspension with no replacement value -- is none (49, 208, 280, 428, 817, 949, 995); 'actually, B' (1, 36, 111, 180, 305, 389, 411, 421, 597, 636, 994) is supersedes, with the hedged 'maybe/what if' twins scored none (24, 44, 164, 206, 476, 663, 734, 878, 1001).

Every quoted, reported, hypothetical, tool-injected and assistant-authored change attempt is none, including 12 that use a correct transition idiom verbatim (33, 62, 103, 171, 213, 274, 339, 356, 441, 559, 661, 811, 950, 984).

The v3 reconciliation test is exercised correctly: inactive target plus changed value gives none + message_new_rule (15, 140, 212, 283, 297, 338, 376, 592, 741, 835, 1019), while unchanged restoration of an inactive version gives reinstates.

The 'Undo that.' low-salience probe appears twice in-file (277, 986) with different targets and once each in kimi-relations and fable-relations-heldout. This is a two-word stock phrase, not a scenario overlap, and no deletion is warranted; recorded so a later dedup pass does not mistake it for contamination. No other message is shared with any file under data/classifier/relations or data/classifier/heldout.
open_ambiguities_recorded_not_patched: row 224 'Forget the saison room-temperature rule for now.' scored none as a 'for-now suspension', against row 248 'Forget the saison room-temperature rule entirely.' scored cancels. v3's none-case is a NARROWER (scope-narrowing) bare suspension; a time-hedged withdrawal covering the target's whole scope is not clearly the same thing. A ruling should be registered before these two are fitted as a minimal pair.

row 1049 'The interior can stay uncovered; I don't care about dust.' scored cancels, and its own why calls it an 'indirect cancellation'; the spec requires an EXPLICIT withdrawal and sends ambiguity to none. This is the weakest cancels in the file.
row 1032 scope=global on a rule whose text is 'for this restoration' (project-wide, not conversation-wide); the task/global line for whole-project rules is not settled in the spec.

rows 986 and 277 ('Undo that.') both resolve to none on ambiguity; 378 ('Undo that three-digit bearing thing, will you?') is cancels because the target is named. The boundary is consistent but rests entirely on the presence of a naming phrase.
summary.coverage: complete for this file's visible content; disjointness from sealed evaluation corpora is asserted by lexical review only, not inspection. Nothing under data/bench or results/quick-checks/focus3-gate was opened.

old_rule: for the telescope review round all ratings to whole stars
message: The telescope review chapter is closed and the whole review task is finished.
why: The message is 'The telescope review chapter is closed and the whole review task is finished.' -- an explicit closure of the WHOLE named task, which is exactly the `completes` definition; the row's own `why` ('sub-unit closure implies but does not finish task') describes a different message. The file scores the identical two-clause shape as completes at 542, 652 and 690 ('...and the whole count is done', '...so we're finished with it'). Genuine sub-unit-only negatives (32, 105, 136, 333, 371, 481, 593, 634, 836, 952, 1014) all lack a whole-task clause.

old_rule: For this headband pattern, always give yardage per colour
message: Great, the headband chart looks clean now, moving on to the matching gloves.
why: The message is 'Great, the headband chart looks clean now, moving on to the matching gloves.' -- praise for a sub-unit plus a task switch, with no closure of the headband pattern task. The row's own `why` says so verbatim ('sub-unit praise plus task switch not closure'). LABELS-RELATIONS v1: a task switch or sub-unit closure alone is none.

old_rule: Withdraw the early-round bye rule for this knockout
message: For this knockout, reinstate the early-round bye rule, please.
why: Status precondition: `reinstates` targets an explicitly inactive version, but this target is status=live -- the only such row in the file (the other 101 reinstates rows target cancelled/completed/superseded). The row is also malformed at the target: `old_rule` is the withdrawal instruction 'Withdraw the early-round bye rule for this knockout', not the rule itself, so there is no original version for `reinstates` to copy. Two repairs are possible; the conservative one, matching the reinstates->none fix at row 130 of kimi-overrides, is to score the row as registered. The alternative (record the bye rule as old_rule with status=cancelled and keep reinstates) requires the author to supply the original rule text and is NOT applied here.

old_rule: Confirm catering numbers with the venue every Tuesday
message: Stop confirming catering numbers each Tuesday; the venue has a standing order now.
why: message_new_rule=True with an empty new_rule_spans list -- the only such row in the file. The message ('Stop confirming catering numbers each Tuesday; the venue has a standing order now.') is a pure cancellation; the trailing clause is a justifying fact, not a persistent instruction. The spec requires verbatim admitted spans whenever message_new_rule is true.

old_rule: Until I say otherwise, italicise every musical number in programmes
message: Reinstate the italics rule for musical numbers, but only in the main-stage programmes.
old: italicise musical numbers in the main-stage programmes

new.text: Reinstate the italics rule for musical numbers, but only in the main-stage programmes.

why: The recorded admitted span 'italicise musical numbers in the main-stage programmes' appears nowhere in the message -- it is a paraphrase, not a quote. v3 requires the verbatim persistent span for a modified restoration and forbids silently discarding the modifier. The whole message is the smallest verbatim unit that carries both the restored requirement and its new scope; this also matches the whole-message admitted spans already used at 140, 297 and 338 for the same modified-restoration family.

The label none is correct; only the rationale is wrong, and a wrong rationale on a hard row misleads the next reviewer.
